captions.detailed: A 3D-printable modular card holder designed for board game cards. It features a thin, flat rectangular base plate with curved cutouts on the front and back edges to allow easy card retrieval. Four L-shaped corner walls extend upwards to keep the deck neatly stacked. The sides of the plate include interlocking dovetail connectors—a female cutout on one side and a matching male tab on the other—enabling multiple holders to slide and lock together side-by-side.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, modular card holder in OpenSCAD with adjustable card dimensions (length, width, and wall height). Include circular thumb cutouts on the front and back edges for easy card removal, and add male/female dovetail connectors on the lateral sides so multiple card trays can lock together.
captions.factory: The design starts with a base plate created using a central `cube`. Circular thumb cutouts are subtracted using two `cylinder` primitives translated along the Y-axis. A female dovetail connector is subtracted from one side of the base plate, and a matching male dovetail is added to the opposite side; both dovetails are constructed using a `difference` of a base `cube` and two rotated `cube` structures to form the angled sides. Finally, the four corner L-walls are assembled by translating and rotating eight individual `cube` primitives (four long walls and four short walls) into position on top of the base plate.
